steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: GCSE RS requires you to understand Christian and Muslim views on the use and abuse of animals, including experimentation, farming and the use of animals for food. | RS Exam Tips — Animal Rights and Experimentation: 1. For Animal Rights and Experimentation questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Animal Rights and Experimentation to its real-world impact on believers and society | UK Context: In the UK, debates about often involve both religious and secular voices.
